edits.title: Diagnose missing biographical fields before further research
edits.content: When structured extraction leaves a biographical field empty, review the stored source specifically for explicit evidence of that field. Distinguish source absence from extraction omission. Do not derive nationality or citizenship from birthplace, education, or workplace. If evidence is absent, retain the unresolved field and search for a source explicitly stating the requested attribute; fetch and verify that evidence before filling the cell. For affiliations, distinguish employment and secondary appointments from educational institutions, and preserve temporal qualifiers such as former or emeritus. Give extraction and review calls the same field definition, temporal scope, and inclusion rules. When the task calls for affiliations recorded in an award announcement, review completeness against that announcement rather than expanding to every outside appointment in a biography. Resolve review findings against the task scope before launching further research. Apply this review to unresolved fields without repeating successful searches or downloads.

edits.title: Prevent later extractions from discarding supported facts
edits.content: A later nationality extraction replaced a validated multi-country value with a single-country mention from another person's page. Schema and quote-membership checks passed; the loss was caught only by comparing with the earlier evidence. Before replacing a populated cell, provide the existing value and supporting evidence alongside new evidence, then compare the proposed change for lost facts. A source mentioning only one component does not disprove other supported components, and a failed corroborating fetch does not invalidate existing evidence. Retain the earlier cell unless stronger evidence justifies the change; resolve genuine conflicts explicitly. Validate proposed replacements before mutating accumulated records.

edits.title: Inspect results and resolve aliases before recording discoveries
edits.content: Empty discovery placeholders caused stalled_search issues even when later calls recorded entities for the same queries. After each search, inspect its results and record actual newly discovered entities once; for search_many, handle each query in input order. Do not emit [] before inspection or assume a later record erases an earlier empty event. Compare entity identities rather than exact name strings: punctuation variants, omitted initials, and contextually established surname-only mentions of known entities are aliases, not new discoveries. Preserve observed spellings in an alias map without merging ambiguous names. Use [] honestly when no new entities were found, including productive searches that verify missing fields for known entities; do not invent discoveries to suppress a stall warning.

edits.title: Recover missing or incomplete fields from rendered evidence
edits.content: When a model-rendered fetch returns usable but incomplete text, identify the specific unresolved fields. Review saved responses first: an extraction may leave a field empty despite available evidence. Track semantic incompleteness as well as empty values; a matching quotation or nonempty cell does not establish complete scope, correct entity attribution, or the required time period. Request concise factual summaries for missing fields and brief supporting excerpts where needed, rather than full-page reproduction. Test a revised focus on one usable page before expanding. Preserve each response with its URL and focus rather than overwriting earlier evidence. For genuinely absent information, use alternative sources instead of inferring from birthplace, institutional location, or ambiguous collective descriptions. When exact wording is required, obtain the complete supported phrase rather than treating a summary or fragment as complete. Keep research-status notes outside factual values. Validate quotations against an individual saved response, then review their support for the entity, field, scope, and relevant time. Supply reviewers the actual contract, including whether quotations must match rendered text or original source text and which fields require historical timing. Repair concrete defects, revalidate changed cells, and stop when no concrete gaps remain. A FETCH_FAILED response calls for bounded retries and source switching, not this incomplete-response procedure.

edits.title: Separate quote membership from factual support
edits.content: A quote occurring in model-rendered fetch output does not by itself establish that it is a source quotation or supports the complete claim. Distinguish source excerpts from renderer summaries, labels and assembled passages; do not reject an actual source heading or excerpt merely because a tool rendered it. Before recording a positive constraint verdict, verify the entity, required time period and every substantive component of the value. Keep extraction and audit criteria aligned with the requested field: explicit national descriptors can support nationality without establishing legal citizenship or dual citizenship. Birthplace, ancestry, workplace, flags and unlinked country labels are insufficient substitutes. Treat model audit findings as hypotheses to resolve against saved evidence and the task contract, not as authoritative corrections. For composite claims, retain a mapping from each component to its source excerpt; never stitch excerpts into a purported verbatim quotation. Recheck semantic support after final mutations, even when schema, substring and coverage checks pass.

edits.title: Repair only unresolved cells from saved evidence
edits.content: When a citation or semantic check fails, reuse saved extractions and fetched text rather than repeating completed research. Track unresolved issues by entity, column and URL. Request patches only for those cells; preserve validated cells unless new evidence identifies a specific defect. Whole-table repair can introduce summary quotations, remove supported fields or retain previously flagged incomplete values. Validate each patch before applying it: check its target, schema, quotation membership in an individual saved retrieval, source provenance and support for the complete value. For one quote with multiple sources, verify it against every cited source; prefer one source supporting the complete value. Removing mismatched sources or narrowing a value may leave a completeness requirement unresolved. Select quotation text directly from saved source strings, preserving punctuation and whitespace. Recheck changed cells and affected coverage after applying patches.

edits.title: Reuse fetched evidence across single and batched research
edits.content: When research mixes single and batched fetching, retain successful fetched text in a URL-keyed dictionary. Deduplicate candidate URLs while preserving order and exclude URLs already cached before calling fetch_many. Associate returned pages with their input URLs, retain usable results, and build extraction evidence directly from the cache. Reuse those same cached strings to check that each extracted citation refers to a supplied URL and contains a verbatim quote. A cache read demonstrates local evidence reuse; it does not establish a backend cache hit. Exercise both single and batched calls only when required or useful for the task.

overflow.diagnosis: Five saved cases ran concurrently against four backend slots. Four direct attempts occupied all slots through their 600-second active timeout. Overflow aggregate deadline included queueing, leaving approximately two seconds at admission. FIFO admitted the waiter before direct retries. Empty worker log is not initialization failure: snapshot.read precedes queueing.
overflow.timing_boundary_note: 46.005 ms joins SI trace exec.end to overflow trace exec.start; these are completion/dispatch events, not an instrumented exact slot-release interval. Consistent with FIFO prompt admission.

host_sleep.interpretation: Confirms clamshell sleep, maintenance/dark wakes and later user wake. Wall time cannot be treated as active planner time; DNS/reset errors fall in that interval. Sleep alone does not establish EPERM cause.

eperm.archived_origin: Host RecordingContext.run_process delegating RunContext.run_process for Codex transport/001, after snapshot.read. Exception message has no stack: Popen versus communication/cleanup remains unlocalized.
eperm.first_probe: Six unmodified local Python processes yielded one Future callback PermissionError at archive.py:114; five caller TimeoutExpired outcomes and one CancelledError. Tool receipt b4b004, raw first output not saved as a separate file.
eperm.instrumented_probe: Three follow-ups reproduce duplicate cleanup 3/3: MainThread killpg succeeds; cancellation callback getpgid sees ESRCH; callback killpg raises EPERM before finished is set.
eperm.confirmed_issue: Timeout cleanup and cancellation callback can signal the same process group concurrently. stop catches only ProcessLookupError, so a real local secondary PermissionError is possible independently of sleep.
eperm.limitation: Local EPERM occurred on callback side and was logged by Future; all instrumented callers retained TimeoutExpired. Original Codex attempt returned PermissionError, so identical throw ordering is unproven. A cleanup-side exception can mask a primary error in the inspected source; that exact replay path is not established.
